draft.title: The respiratory system
card: The respiratory system moves air into and out of the body. Air travels in through the nose or mouth, then down the trachea, into the bronchi and on to smaller tubes called bronchioles.
The bronchioles end in tiny air sacs called alveoli. Each alveolus is wrapped in tiny blood vessels called capillaries.
Gas exchange happens at the alveoli. Oxygen passes from the air into the blood. Carbon dioxide, a waste gas made by the cells, passes from the blood into the air.
The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle under the lungs. When it contracts, the chest gets bigger and air is drawn in. The carbon dioxide is then breathed out.
draft.remember: Air travels down the airways to the alveoli, where oxygen goes into the blood and carbon dioxide comes out.

a.q: Where does oxygen pass from the air into the blood?
opts: In the alveoli
In the trachea
In the bronchi
In the diaphragm
a.why: Gas exchange happens at the alveoli, where thin walls sit next to the capillaries. The trachea and bronchi only carry air to the alveoli, so no oxygen enters the blood there.
a.clue: Look for the tiny air sacs wrapped in capillaries.

b.q: Jas finishes a sprint and breathes out hard. Which gas is moving from her blood into the air in her alveoli to be breathed out?
opts: Carbon dioxide, a waste gas from her cells
Oxygen, which her cells have finished using
Carbon dioxide, which her cells need for energy
Oxygen, which her blood has too much of
b.why: Cells make carbon dioxide as a waste gas. It moves from the blood into the alveoli and is breathed out. Oxygen moves the other way, from the air into the blood.
b.clue: Which gas is the waste that leaves the blood?

b.best: Carbon dioxide, a waste gas from her cells

problems.detail: "The carbon dioxide is then breathed out" follows the sentence on the diaphragm contracting. It does not say that breathing out happens when the diaphragm relaxes and the chest gets smaller. It could also suggest that breathed-out air is only carbon dioxide, when it still holds a lot of oxygen and nitrogen.

card: The respiratory system moves air into and out of the body. Air travels in through the nose or mouth, then down the trachea, into the bronchi and on to smaller tubes called bronchioles.
The bronchioles end in tiny air sacs called alveoli. Alveoli have very thin walls, and each one is wrapped in tiny blood vessels called capillaries.
Gas exchange happens at the alveoli. Oxygen passes from the air into the blood. Carbon dioxide, a waste gas made by the cells, passes from the blood into the air.

The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle under the lungs. When it contracts, the chest gets bigger and air is drawn in. When it relaxes, the chest gets smaller and air is pushed out, carrying carbon dioxide but still holding plenty of oxygen and nitrogen.
